newsitem.title: INDIA: India rulers, Congress start crisis talks.
newsitem.headline: India rulers, Congress start crisis talks.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition and the Congress party on Wednesday began formal talks to resolve an 11-day-old political crisis threatening the government's survival, the Press Trust of India said.

The news agency said negotiations had begun at the New Delhi residence of Farooq Abdullah, the chief minister of Jammu and Kashmir state. It said the coalition's negotiators had spoken to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda before the meeting began.

The alliance named a three-member panel for the talks, comprising Abdullah, Harkishan Singh Surjeet, general secretary of the Communist Party of India-Marxist and Andhra Pradesh state Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu, United Front officials said.
It was not clear who was representing Congress at the talks. Congress officials earlier said it would be at least a day before the situation cleared.

News that the two sides were preparing for talks raised hopes that they could resolve their differences before a vote of confidence in parliament set for Friday, and sent the Bombay Stock Exchange's benchmark 30-share index surging 131.80 points, or 3.74 percent, to end at a provisional 3,652.29 close.

Congress party president Sitaram Kesri sparked the crisis on March 30 when he announced the withdrawal of his party's vital support for Deve Gowda's minority centre-left coalition. Kesri has demanded that Deve Gowda step down but the United Front has rejected the demand.
